observations.why: First-person plural with a decisive verb enacts a collective decision under the speaker's authority — 'we' as a body directed by the speaker, not a peer proposal.
Proportionality framing — the switch is justified by quantified benefit-to-cost ratio, the relational logic of market-pricing.
Memo header asserts a migration as decided fact, enacting authority-ranking through declarative allocation rather than proposal.
Quantified performance gain restated as proportionality — benefit measured in multiples, the cost/benefit logic of market-pricing.
Setting a timeline is a rank-based allocation of time — the speaker (or memo) imposes a schedule, enacting authority-ranking.
